data.name: The Life and Suffering of Sir Brante
data.detailed_description:
NEW GAME OUT NOW!


JOIN THE COMMUNITY ON DISCORD


Acerca do jogo

The Life and Suffering of Sir Brante é um RPG narrativo implacável que ganha vida através das páginas do diário do protagonista. Situada em um mundo onde qualquer forma de rebeldia é impiedosamente repreendida, a história acompanha um homem que ousou desafiar a ordem vigente. Embarque em uma jornada para se tornar um indivíduo capaz de criar seu próprio destino. Mas lembre-se: a liberdade sempre tem seu preço.

A vida no Grande Império Akniano é dura, e sua casta ao nascer é a mais prejudicada. Você é um plebeu, sem direitos e sem títulos. Para comandar seu destino e se tornar o herdeiro legítimo do legado da família Brante, você terá que enfrentar uma tradição rígida e o preconceito. Embarque na jornada de uma vida, desde o nascimento até a verdadeira morte, enfrentando grandes levantes, encarando adversidades e tomando decisões difíceis. Cada uma afeta não apenas o protagonista, sua família e seus amigos, mas poderá derrubar as estruturas que sustentam o próprio Império.

Destaques

Na virada do tempo

A vida de todos os cidadãos imperiais é predeterminada pelos seus feudos. As divindades conhecidas como os Deuses Gêmeos impuseram essa verdade ao mundo, dividindo os mortais em castas. Os nobres governam sobre os outros, os clérigos guiam as pessoas pelo caminho da verdade, e os plebeus sofrem, trabalhando arduamente em nome da glória do Império. Você pode aceitar seu destino sem questionar, mas também está em seu poder alterar a ordem cósmica que governa a todos.


Sua escolha não é uma ilusão

O jogo é dividido em capítulos, acompanhando as ações do jogador, as habilidades adquiridas e outras circunstâncias, formando uma trama distinta em cada sessão de jogo. Cada decisão tem suas consequências, e você será responsável por toda a jornada. Proteger sua família e amigos, impor a ordem do Imperador e ganhar uma fortuna ou tentar mudar o mundo... Faça sua escolha, mas cuidado com os perigos do orgulho e da ambição.


Lute pela sua vida

Nenhum homem é onipotente, mas Sir Brante pode, com sua orientação, se tornar capaz de resistir às provações do destino e de reescrever as leis que governam este mundo! Desenvolva e treine seu personagem, aprimorando características como determinação, sensibilidade e resistência. Todas as habilidades do herói, a começar pelas adquiridas na infância, afetarão a personalidade, a visão de mundo e os relacionamentos dele, abrindo caminho para novos talentos e possíveis tramas na história.

Encontre o seu caminho

A primeira sessão de jogo pode levar até 15 horas! Diversas ramificações na história tornam cada experiência de jogo única: vire um nobre juiz, aprenda o caminho da inquisição, agite uma revolução como membro de uma sociedade secreta ou dedique-se a um propósito totalmente diferente. Demonstre coragem e o destino cederá aos seus desígnios!


Para todo o sempre

O sistema de ressurreição possibilita que o personagem mantenha a experiência ao morrer, permitindo que o jogador reavalie decisões passadas e faça ajustes à estratégia no futuro. Controle sua vida e sua morte, e assuma riscos neste ciclo de morte e renascimento!

data.short_description: Um RPG narrativo implacável, situado em um mundo governado por deuses reais e impiedosos. Embarque em uma jornada desafiadora em que cada escolha tem um preço e consequência. Você vai se tornar um inquisidor? Um juiz? Ou vai conspirar contra a velha ordem? A decisão é sua!

reviews.review:
[h2]TLDR:[/h2] An intriguing narrative adventure that doesn't pull its punches and makes the player ... well, suffer.

[h2]GAMEPLAY OVERVIEW:[/h2] The Life and Suffering of Sr Brante (SirB) is a narrative adventure following the life of the player as they fill the role of the the middle son of the Brante family. 

Gameplay proceeds by presenting scenarios to the player and asking for choices. The game is not real-time, and there are no quick-time events, so the player can read and digest all the information before deciding. Some decisions have pre-existing conditions before being available.

The player accumulates stats based on decisions, which will unlock further choices. The stats from the first two chapters (Childhood and Youth) combine to give the stats used through the remaining of the game. For example, Determination from Childhood and Nobility from Youth give the player their starting Valor score in Chapter 3 (Adolescence). The player will also need to build relationships with their family members and other NPCs. The family has overall reputation, unity, and wealth scores. There are similar meters for the province itself. All of this may sound overwhelming but it becomes easy to navigate after playing for a short time.

Events come in two flavors. The first type is static, which occur at the same point during each playthrough, involving background events that affect the city of Anizotte, the empire, and the player's relationships. The second are special events that only occur when the player has a stat or a character relationship high or low enough to trigger. Special events will often have a lasting effect on the game's direction.

Death is an occasional danger. In this world, the player can die up to three "lesser" deaths, meaning they are briefly in the afterlife before returning to the world. A fourth death results in "true" death and the end of life. Lesser deaths often offer large stat or relationship rewards. As with everything else in the game, choosing a lesser death is a trade-off. True death can occur early, usually from making enemies of powerful foes, so be careful.

Assuming the character doesn't die a true death by the end of the fourth chapter (a distinct possibility), the fifth chapter covers the revolution in Anizotte where, as usual, the player's history and choices affect the outcome of not only the city but the entire empire.

The suffering part of SirB is no joke. Regardless of the path the player picks, there are always some very hard decisions to be made, with no good answers. Some seemingly-innocuous choices can come back to haunt the player much later. It also means you can be hard-locked into choices you otherwise wouldn't make. Most of the times, those railroaded decisions make logical sense, if not for enjoyable gameplay. Suffering, indeed.

I really made a hash of my first game. I died twice, broke the church, ruined the province, left my family in tatters, ensured the revolution ended in bloody stalemate, and had to flee the city in shame ... and given what happened in some other runs, it could have been worse. It is possible to get mostly positive endings, though doing so involves a tightrope of choices that are not always obvious.

Fortunately, it's easy to click past a lot of the narrative on subsequent playthroughs. I recommend reading and enjoying the first few times, and then fast-forwarding past events already seen. If one is clicking through, a whole run can be done in an hour and a half or so. Also, players can reload and play forward from the start of any chapter, so mistakes don't have to tank a whole game.

[h2]STORY / WORLDBUILDING:[/h2] SirB sets up a rather intriguing world, very reminiscent of early-Renaissance Europe. The empire, run by the noble families of the non-human Arkians, enforces a strict class system between the nobles and commoners, called "lots." The lot of the nobles is to rule, the lot of the commoners to toil and suffer, after which they will be rewarded in the afterlife by the Twins, the gods of the world, for conforming to their lots. There is also the priest lot, whose job is to spread the word of the Twins. Naturally, much of the game's conflict revolves around the conflict between these lots, and the player's decisions about them.

The NPCs with whom the player interacts bring a variety of relationships. The player's family members, a childhood friend, romantic interests, religious figures both forgiving and stern, sinister spymasters, haughty noblemen, and idealistic judges ... all of them are distinct and unique in the setting. I had a lot of fun trying to maximize good relationships and positive endings with different groups of them, since it's just not possible to achieve a global good ending for everyone in a single playthrough.

The story depends on the player's actions and every path the player chooses—noble, commoner, or priest—has multiple outcomes, all of which have positive or negative implications for the various NPCs. I ran through about eight full runs and experienced near-perfect happiness, complete disasters, and everything in between.

[h2]TECHNICAL ASPECTS:[/h2] Brante loaded quickly and ran without glitches or crashes. The plain graphics and scrawling style of unfolding story as events happen works for the gameplay. Sound is similarly minimalist and effective, and I thought light musical score was perfect for the game's ambiance.

I did notice the game trip up several times, such as mentioning a character that has "heard of" the player, after they've already had direct interaction. This type of error is common in these games, though, and it only cropped up here and there. There were also a handful of typos in the story narrative, such as one line reading, "Thous halt," instead of "Thou shalt."

Steam achievements will take a while, as many are exclusive to the paths the player takes in life. It will take multiple runs to 100% this one, though as mentioned above, later runs can be cycled through pretty quickly.

[h2]FINAL WORD:[/h2] SirB spins a pretty fun tale, with decent replay value.

[h2]SCORE: 7.5/10[/h2]
